summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of niobium silicide (NbSi) films using NbF5 and Si2H6 as precursors. The ALD process was optimized to achieve a high growth rate and uniform films with a 1:1 stoichiometry. The films were found to be metallic and superconducting below 3.1 K. The study also highlights the importance of surface conditions and the effect of post-deposition annealing on the superconducting properties of the films.
